html:
Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is a Nigerian writer whose novels and talks have reached readers around the world. Her novel Half of a Yellow Sun (2006) retold the Nigerian Civil War over Biafra for a global audience.

She was born in Enugu to an Igbo family and grew up in the university town of Nsukka, in a house once lived in by Chinua Achebe, whom she counts as a key influence. At nineteen she left to study in the United States.

  • Purple Hibiscus (2003) tells of a girl growing up under a violent, devout father.
  • Half of a Yellow Sun follows several people through the Biafran war of 1967 to 1970, in which her grandfathers died. It won the Orange Prize in 2007.
  • Americanah (2013) is about a Nigerian woman in America and Britain, and about what race means there.

Her talk "The Danger of a Single Story" (2009) warned against seeing Africa or anyone through one story. Another, "We Should All Be Feminists", became a short book and was sampled by Beyoncé. She is one of the best-known voices of a new generation of African writers.
sum: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is a Nigerian writer whose novels and talks have reached readers around the world. Her novel Half of a Yellow Sun (2006) retold the Nigerian Civil War over Biafra for a global audience.
